**8B.2 Research Note: Ali Khamenei, 2024**

**Bottom line**
Partly yes, but weakly and unevenly. Khamenei did translate parts of his 2024 program into concrete institutional moves, mainly through loyalist vetting, approved appointments, and selective enforcement in the nuclear file. I did not find strong evidence of a transparent budgeted implementation plan, timelines, or a detailed public policy architecture for the “resistance economy” beyond slogans and personnel control.

**Positive / partial translation**

- [Khamenei and Raisi Speeches on Nowruz](https://iranprimer.usip.org/index.php/blog/2024/mar/21/khamenei-and-raisi-speeches-nowruz) | The Iran Primer / USIP | 2024-03-21  
  Claim: Khamenei said the economy was Iran’s “main weakness,” named domestic production as the fix for inflation, jobs, and currency weakness, and said foreign agreements should be turned into “national executive contracts” with tangible results. This is the clearest sign of a governing program being expressed in actionable priorities, though still not in a budgeted implementation plan.  
  IDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- [Iran's presidential election dominated by Khamenei loyalists](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/irans-presidential-election-dominated-by-khamenei-loyalists-3494879) | Reuters | 2024-06-25  
  Claim: Reuters said Khamenei ensured hardline candidates dominated the contest and that the Guardian Council approved only five hardliners and one low-profile moderate from 80 applicants. That is concrete personnel control, showing the program was translated into elite selection and regime-management mechanisms.  
  IDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.9`, `7B.8`

- [Pezeshkian Cabinet Profiles](https://iranprimer.usip.org/index.php/blog/2024/aug/22/pezeshkian-cabinet-profiles) | The Iran Primer / USIP | 2024-08-22  
  Claim: The new cabinet included reformists, hardliners, technocrats, and academics, and the list reportedly had Khamenei, IRGC, and security-agency approval before submission. That is evidence of a translated staffing process, but it looks compromise-driven rather than like a fully specified policy program.  
  IDs: `8B.2`, `7B.5`, `7B.8`, `7B.9`

- [Iran will not impede IAEA access, head of its atomic organisation says](https://theprint.in/world/iran-will-not-impede-iaea-access-head-of-its-atomic-organisation-says/2403254/) | Reuters | 2024-12-14  
  Claim: Iran said it would not obstruct IAEA access and would operate within safeguards. This is a late-year procedural commitment showing that the nuclear line was translated into a concrete institutional posture, even if narrowly and conditionally.  
  IDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`, `7B.6`

- [Tehran signals no retaliation against Israel after drones attack](https://www.theprint.in/world/tehran-signals-no-retaliation-against-israel-after-drones-attack/2048236/) | Reuters | 2024-04-19  
  Claim: Tehran downplayed the Isfahan incident and said it had no retaliation plan, which Reuters said appeared aimed at averting regional war. This is tactical translation of restraint into operational behavior, but it was short-lived.  
  IDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`

**Negative / weak translation**

- [Iran holds presidential vote with limited choices](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iran-holds-presidential-vote-with-limited-choices-3500514) | Reuters | 2024-06-27  
  Claim: Reuters said voter apathy was driven by economic hardship and social restrictions, and that candidates avoided concrete economic plans even while acknowledging the crisis. That is evidence against a serious implementation pipeline: slogans were present, but concrete planning was thin.  
  IDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.8`

- [IAEA board passes resolution against Iran on cooperation, inspectors](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iaea-board-passes-resolution-against-iran-on-cooperation-inspectors-3472087) | Reuters | 2024-06-05  
  Claim: Iran barred many experienced inspectors, and the IAEA Board demanded reversal. That undercuts any claim that the program was being implemented through durable, rules-based institutions; the mechanism was noncooperation, not disciplined execution.  
  IDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.6`, `7B.7`

- [Iran leader Khamenei, rifle at his side, vows resistance against Israel](https://theprint.in/world/iran-leader-khamenei-rifle-at-his-side-vows-resistance-against-israel/2297444/) | Reuters | 2024-10-04  
  Claim: Khamenei framed resistance against Israel as non-negotiable and said strikes served the region and humanity. This is a clear strategic line, but it still reads more like mobilizing rhetoric than a detailed program translated into institutions or budgets.  
  IDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`

- [Iran says nuclear weapons have no place in its nuclear doctrine](https://www.yahoo.com/news/iran-says-nuclear-weapons-no-085328983.html) | Reuters | 2024-04-22  
  Claim: Iran publicly denied a nuclear-weapons role in doctrine, and Reuters noted Khamenei’s long-standing fatwa. This is a formal commitment, but it remained mostly declaratory rather than embedded in a visible implementation architecture.  
  IDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`, `7B.10`

**Synthesis**
- Concrete translation exists most clearly in:
  - loyalist vetting and candidate control
  - cabinet approval and personnel balancing
  - IAEA-safeguards posture and selective restraint
- Weak points:
  - little evidence of published budgets
  - little evidence of detailed timelines
  - little evidence of transparent policy instruments beyond speeches and elite control
- Overall: Khamenei’s 2024 program was translated into institutions and appointments more than into a public, budgeted governing plan.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a direct 2024 source showing a Khamenei-authored budget, formal implementation timetable, or a detailed operational plan for the “resistance economy.”
- The public record is much stronger on rhetoric, elite selection, and coercive enforcement than on explicit administrative planning.
